the precision/recall of multiattribute extraction is a computationally hard problem.

there are trade-offs between the computational efficiency, precision and recall of data extraction algorithms and the formalization proposed in this paper can be used to analyze and design algorithms to achieve the desired precision-recall-complexity tradeoff.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a formalism to characterize the precision and recall of data extraction from semisructured data sources.
the formalism we propose provides a framework for studying the impact of learning algorithms on the precision and recall of data extraction from semistru c tured sources.
we have proposed a formalization of the precision and recall of data extraction, and investigated their complexity theoretic aspects.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the choice of a learning algorithm for data extraction can have a significant impact on the quality of the extracted data and that the choice should be guided by the application requirements and the characteristics of the data source.
precision and recall are not independent metrics, rather there is a strong correlation between them.
learning algorithms can be designed to achieve high recall with low precision, or low recall with high precision, depending on the application requirements.
